To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we show that the performance of the state-of-the-art word vector models can be improved by using graded weighting of the word vectors in building the document vectors, and (b) we show that such improvements can be further boosted by using ensemble learning.
we have developed a novel approach to the problem of composing document vectors, and that this approach is effective on several datasets in multiple languages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
building composite document vectors from words and phrases, using a weighted scheme for word selection and composition.
developing a better understanding of document composition and the role of stop words.
the development of a new model for building composite document vectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed models are language free models that can be used in an unsupervized manner and are applicable to all the languages.
our approach, which uses a combination of tf-idf and RNN, is able to outperform all other methods on both the IMDB and Amazon datasets.
the tf-idf weighting model is a simple and robust approach for building composite document vectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the word vector based approaches are indeed very effective for document classification and we can improve the performance further by using the graded weightings.
we propose a new model for document vector representation which is based on the idea of weighted word vectors.
we have proposed a new model for document representation which is a combination of tf-idf weighting scheme with the matrix-vector composition of word vectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a graded approach is more suitable than the binary yes-no approach for the problem of document composition.
a simple model such as tf-idf can result in an improvement of 2-3% in performance, and a combination of such methods with an ensemble approach can result in an even better performance.
a graded weighting model is a more effective way of composing word vectors than the simple average or other matrix vector approaches.
